title: Riverwalk North workshop lays out roughly $8 million plan, EPA cleanup grant
blurb: The board also approved a fourth extension for a building addition at 860 Spring Street. It recommended folding Village Review design oversight into its own process.

title: Council finalizes data centers ban; Rec Commission vote draws more public comment
blurb: Also: the City joins a nationwide fire-truck price-fixing lawsuit. Two items passed first reading, the first of two votes: selling a riverside parcel to a longtime leaseholder for $50,000, and a new union contract for a newly split city bargaining unit (a group of workers under one union contract). Final votes are set for Nov. 16.
hotNote: Contested

title: Rec Commission rename sparks the sharpest floor fight in months
blurb: Also: a data center ban advances, a new Saccarappa Park deal, Halloween road closure, and several quieter items passed without debate.
hotNote: Contested

title: Social media attack on student athletes draws united community response
blurb: Also: the Support Staff contract is ratified. A $38,650 emergency fire-alarm repair won first approval. A Siemens energy-efficiency study that could lead to $3–6 million in projects moved forward after close review.

title: Public speakers object to Stroudwater Meadows access road
blurb: The board also recommended the City's new data-center ban. It gave a Rock Row subdivision more time to be recorded. It kept a Rock Row apartment-and-garage plan open for more design work.
hotNote: Stroudwater Meadows — sharp public pushback on access road

title: Council confirms Bruno Inácio as Finance Director
blurb: Also: the Council approved buying portable traffic signals, which are expected to save about $15,000 a year in flagger wages. It also renewed the General Assistance maximums.

title: Committee of the Whole moves the latest boards-and-committees review to the full Council
blurb: The amended ordinance heads to the full Council. Staff also plan a one-year report-back, separate from the ordinance text.

title: Special meeting with four of seven members fills three staff jobs
blurb: Four of seven members were present. They approved three staff nominations without debate. These were an interim assistant principal, a one-year assistant director of special services, and an occupational therapist.

title: Public-comment rule change splits Council 4–2 over ward disclosure
blurb: Speakers no longer have to state their home address. The change passed over objections from Councilors Chau and McCambridge.
hotNote: Ward-disclosure amendment, 4–2 split (McCambridge, Chau opposed)

title: Committee sends changes for seven boards to the full Council and sets aside the Public Safety Commission review
blurb: Amendments for seven boards go to the Council to consider. They are the Board of Assessment Review, Woodlawn Cemetery Trustees, Fair Hearing Authority, Library Advisory Committee, Zoning Board of Appeals, Planning Board, and Village Review Overlay Zone Committee.

title: Council passes first of two votes on Teamsters General Unit contract
blurb: Also: early reports on the Student Transit Pass Program are positive. The Council also voted on several routine grants and equipment purchases.

title: Planning Board weighs staff plan to drop data centers from Rock Row's zoning
blurb: The board also approved a three-lot subdivision on Longfellow Street and looked at a new "social engagement" design ordinance.

title: Chair pushes back after a board member criticizes teachers' classroom wish lists on Facebook
blurb: Also: 19 teacher/administrator hires are approved, and the high school rolls out Yonder pouches and Metro bus passes for the new school year.
hotNote: No split vote, but sustained board conflict over a member's Facebook criticism of teachers' donation wish lists

title: The Planning Board extends Kidder Lane approval and OKs Kia and Marco Commons plans, all unanimous
blurb: Workshops looked at a parking expansion on Larrabee Road, a redesigned project on Conant Street, and a new subdivision on Longfellow Street.

title: Transit-pass program passes 5–2 after an hours-long debate over a disputed bus route
blurb: An amendment to send the Monroe Avenue route change to committee failed 2–5. A separate project, Riverwalk North, drew long-standing opposition from neighbors whose land borders it.
hotNote: Hours-long transit-pass debate (2–5 failed amendment, 5–2 final) + Riverwalk North abutter opposition

title: After seven years with co-principals, the high school has one principal and two assistant principals
blurb: Also: City-funded Greater Portland Metro bus passes for high school students await a final City Council vote. Three administrator nominations passed unanimously.

title: Student Transit Pass Program clears first reading 6–1 after extended debate
blurb: Free Metro bus passes for Westbrook High School students drew concerns over cost, safety, and a new Monroe Avenue stop.
hotNote: Student Transit Pass Program, 6–1 first-reading split

title: Committee of the Whole opens review of the City's boards and committees
blurb: A plan to drop ward-specific seats drew pushback over representation for Westbrook's poorer wards. No vote was taken.

title: Millbrook Estates affordable housing wins final approval, 3–1
blurb: Chair McWilliams voted no on design grounds. The board also reviewed early plans for a Bill Dodge Kia renovation and two Rock Row buildings.
hotNote: Millbrook Estates final vote, 3–1 split (McWilliams dissent)

title: Council previews free student transit passes and a plan to update the laws on its boards
blurb: Millbrook Estates' tax increment financing items passed with no public comment. A sewer repair order passed first reading after talk about grease traps.

title: Planning Board workshops updated plans for the former Twin Falls golf course
blurb: A 228-unit housing redevelopment across seven buildings drew only two remote comments. A routine site-plan extension also passed unanimously.

title: Tennis court repair item splits Council 5–1 amid Millbrook Estates TIF pushback
blurb: Eleven new-business orders moved forward, most of them unanimously. The meeting also had a Juneteenth proclamation and a talk on residential growth trends.
hotNote: Tennis-court item 5–1 split + Millbrook Estates TIF public pushback

title: FY27 school budget passes with 70% voter approval and unusually high turnout
blurb: Teachers of the Year and retirees with 211 combined years of service were honored. A one-year change to special-education leadership was proposed.

title: Millbrook Estates affordable housing draws criticism from a resident and the Chair at a long meeting
blurb: The board also approved three other projects. It reviewed early plans for a new Element by Marriott hotel at Rock Row.
hotNote: Millbrook Estates criticism from a resident and the Chair + 955 Bridgton Rd opposition, marathon 3.5-hr meeting

title: Council passes a moratorium on data centers
blurb: The meeting also paid tribute to former City Administrator Jerry Bryant on his retirement. Data-center zoning rules were sent to the Planning Board to study.

title: Planning Board previews Rock Row's first Phase 3 buildings
blurb: A 7-story parking garage with ground-floor shops and a 6-story, ~276-unit residential building drew mostly positive early feedback.

title: Fire Chief previews new opioid-overdose EMS pilot program
blurb: Also: a Memorial Day parade permit, an overnight water-utility street closure, and Westbrook Together Days road closures.

title: Cell-phone ban and Yonder pouch funding both pass 5–1, Poitras dissenting on safety grounds
blurb: Also: seven retirements were announced. The district said the FY27 budget passed City Council and now goes to a referendum.
hotNote: Split 5–1 votes on cell-phone ban policy (JICJ) and Yonder pouch funding, both Poitras dissenting on safety

title: Hammond Road garage variance approved; no one spoke against it
blurb: The Chair and Vice Chair were both absent, so the board chose an interim Vice Chair. It then approved a rear-setback variance for an attached garage by a show of hands, after going through the seven required criteria.

title: Stroudwater Meadows housing project draws heavy traffic opposition
blurb: Three large residential projects were workshopped in one unusually packed meeting; two more items ran out of time.
hotNote: Stroudwater Meadows — ~13 speakers, extensive traffic opposition

title: Rooster ban passes 5–1 after dueling public comment
blurb: The FY2026–27 budget then passed 6–0. Rairdon, the lone April dissenter, was absent.
hotNote: Rooster ordinance 5–1 split (Turcotte) ×2 + heated school-budget public comment

title: Revised FY27 budget gets final approval as City Council votes the same evening
blurb: A short special meeting gave final approval to a $136,295.39 cut tied to the School Resource Officer cost shift. There was no discussion.

title: School Committee gives first approval to $136,295 budget cut as City moves to absorb full cost of School Resource Officers
blurb: A short special meeting gives first-reading approval (the first of two votes) to lower figures in three budget questions, called warrant articles. This follows the City Council's first-reading vote to move the full School Resource Officer cost into the public safety budget.

title: FY2026–27 budget passes first reading, 5–1, with Rairdon dissenting
blurb: The Council also advanced several paving and infrastructure bid awards and entered executive session on a legal matter.
hotNote: Budget first reading, 5–1 split (Rairdon), sharp public pushback

title: FY27 budget adopted as teachers plead to save two cut instructional-coach positions
blurb: Also: Chair Mancuso speaks in her individual capacity against a proposed state bill on school sports and gender identity.

title: FY27 budget clears first reading at 7.5%, down from the original 9.88% proposal
blurb: Also: three staff retirements are announced and Mayor Morse voices confidence in the Council's continued full support for the school budget.

title: Finance Subcommittee recommends a 7.5% budget increase after a surprise health-insurance windfall
blurb: Also: School Committee Chair Andrea Mancuso confirms a formal request asking the City to absorb School Resource Officer costs entirely.

title: Planning Board approves 11-unit Pierce Street project, 4–1, over drainage concerns
blurb: The board also approved the Redeemer Church relocation and got its first look at Rock Row's Phase 3 master plan.
hotNote: 4–1 split vote

title: Firefighters' union disputes City's staffing statement, backs Chief Sloan's first interview
blurb: The Mayor gave the FY2026–27 budget address. The Council tabled (set aside) a rooster-ban ordinance over a disputed enclosure-size requirement.
hotNote: Firefighters' union vs. City on minimum staffing (no vote)

title: Finance Subcommittee cuts two secondary instructional coaches in a split tally as members say the City isn't carrying its share
blurb: Also: proposed professional development and supply cuts meet real pushback.
hotNote: Sharp City-funding-fairness exchange; 4–2 tally cuts two secondary coaches, English teacher & Tier 2 coaches left open

title: Finance Chair says she's “not comfortable” with a 9.88% increase, orders more cuts
blurb: Also: $23,000 is added to fix the middle-school bathroom locks. A newly disclosed possible data breach at the district's student-information vendor adds weight to the cybersecurity hire.
hotNote: Chair: “not comfortable with a 9.88 percent” increase, orders more cuts; ongoing City-charge frustration; Compass relocation process criticism

title: “I will have a hard time supporting this budget” — School Committee Chair presses on middle-school bathroom privacy
blurb: Also: a new committee member challenges School Resource Officer funding. The district again presses the City on its $121,000 field-maintenance charge.
hotNote: Middle school bathroom-privacy fix (“I will have a hard time supporting this budget”), SRO funding challenged, $121K city field charge pushback

title: Finance Subcommittee digs into a special-education funding mechanism that “broke my brain”
blurb: Also: the multilingual program serves the third-largest population in Maine. Prices for classroom supplies are spiking districtwide.

title: Finance Subcommittee's first budget-review night zeroes in on a $121,000 city field-maintenance charge
blurb: Also: a cybersecurity hire is requested to end the district's “single point of failure.” New pottery wheels are sought for a booming ceramics program.

title: Mayor marks Finance Director Tressina Germani's departure after nearly 14 years
blurb: Also adopted a Food Security Grant Program ordinance and an ambulance debt write-off policy. Gave first-reading approval to Riverwalk North permitting and design funding.

title: State of the Schools: special-education enrollment climbs to a county-high 27%
blurb: Also: the FY27 budget calendar is set, and the 2026-27 school calendar drops the staggered kindergarten start for this year. Chair Mancuso reports she met with Governor Mills about school funding.

title: Finance Subcommittee opens budget season with a 9.88% proposed increase
blurb: Also: the district's energy-efficiency project is projected to beat its $255,000 savings guarantee, and a new Pre-K program takes shape.

title: Planning Board approves Prompto Oil Change site plan, previews Redeemer Church relocation
blurb: The board also recommended approval of the updated child-care ordinance language. None of the votes were contested.

title: Council hears FY2025 audit's clean opinion, caught in a Bucket Brigade dispute
blurb: Twelve people spoke about a dispute between the Westbrook Bucket Brigade and the Historical Society's leadership. Routine capital and school funding items moved forward.

title: Council remembers former Councilor John O'Hara and moves the FY26 Capital Improvement Plan forward
blurb: Firefighters urged the Council to restore funding for a regional fire training facility. The plan included nearly $2 million in new general obligation bonds.

title: FY25 audit comes back clean as the district launches its own Pre-K program
blurb: Also: a request to move bond money goes to City Council. Six School Department policies passed first approval in one vote.

title: Board hears hours-long appeal over a cannabis caregiver's "retail" lines
blurb: Stroudwater General's owner appealed a notice of violation. The notice says the business outgrew its grandfathered caregiver-cultivation status. The board leaned toward upholding the notice but took no final vote. The matter was continued to March 24.
hotNote: Sharp credibility challenge to the Code Enforcement Officer ("disingenuous"), extensive board disagreement, no final vote yet

title: Planning Board approves early tree-clearing phase for Buddhist temple project
blurb: The board also elected 2026 officers. It previewed a warehouse addition and new child-care ordinance language.

title: Council previews a PFAS testing agreement with GPCOG
blurb: Also: two new liquor licenses passed, a business personal-property-tax outreach program was announced, and Community Development Block Grant applications were endorsed.

title: Committee of the Whole leaves remote-participation policy unchanged
blurb: A short, one-item workshop with no public comment. The board took no further action on the item sent to it.

title: Westbrook expands halal-certified school meals districtwide
blurb: Also: subcommittee assignments were set, a new recruiting video for the Westbrook Regional Vocational Center debuted, and the committee met in private on a personnel matter.

title: Rifle suppressor purchase for police passes 6–1 after sharp debate
blurb: The Council also got an early update on PFAS at three city-owned parcels. It also approved election clerks and a Zoning Board of Appeals alternate.
hotNote: Suppressor purchase, 6–1 split (Munro) + forceful public debate

title: Foster Street parking dispute splits Council 5–1
blurb: Also: good news on next year's workers' comp costs, a Town Line Diner liquor license was approved, and the Mayor raised a holiday trash-pickup breakdown.
hotNote: Foster St. parking, 5–1 split (Rairdon)
